In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the priority scheme is effective to support multiple QOs classes in IPv6 over the ATM network.
the priority scheme is a good approach to support different QoS classes, but the network should be designed with a sufficient capacity to accommodate the background traffic.

, the priority scheme can provide better performance in terms of cell loss rate and delay when there is a large amount of background traffic, however, it can be detrimental to the performance of low priority traffic when there is little or no background traffic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the multi-priority IPv6 scheme over ATM networks is feasible and effective.
we have shown the effectiveness of the multi-priority mechanism in IPv6 running on ATM networks.
the multi-priority mechanism in IPv6 can be used to provide QoS support to the network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the multi-priority traffic can coexist with best-effort traffic without much performance degradation.
the priority mechanism can be used to enhance the overall performance of the network, but it is not a panacea for all problems.
the priority scheme is effective in providing the desired QoS for the traffic that has been given the highest priority.
